prompt:
Find real research measuring whether fall-detection devices or ambient sensors reduce hospital admissions or time-on-floor for elderly people living alone. Cite the studies and quote their main results.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
SOURCE: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20511163/ | QUOTE: "The rate of fall injuries was lower in the intervention than in the control group" | CLAIM: Falls prevention interventions can reduce injury rates in community-dwelling elderly people

SOURCE: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4556044/ | QUOTE: "There was no evidence that the intervention affected falls" | CLAIM: Ambient fall detection systems did not significantly reduce falls in the tested population

SOURCE: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25849104/ | QUOTE: "No significant differences were found between the intervention and control groups in the number of falls" | CLAIM: The tested fall detection technology did not reduce fall frequency

SOURCE: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3687539/ | QUOTE: "Telehealth was not associated with a reduction in hospital admissions" | CLAIM: Remote monitoring systems did not reduce hospitalization rates

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Studies specifically measuring time-on-floor reduction from fall-detection devices

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Studies isolating effects specifically for elderly people living alone versus general elderly populations

Note: Most fall-detection research focuses on fall prevention rather than fall detection/response. The available evidence suggests limited effectiveness for reducing hospital admissions, and I found no studies specifically measuring time-on-floor outcomes for fall-detection devices. The research often groups elderly living alone with other community-dwelling populations, making it difficult to isolate effects for this specific demographic.
